summary.one_liner: duf is a colorful, terminal-based disk usage and free-space utility for Linux, BSD, macOS and Windows, offering a friendlier alternative to df.
summary.what_it_does: duf lists mounted devices and mount points with their size, used and available space, and usage percentage, in a colorful table that adapts to the terminal's theme and width. It can be run with no arguments to show all relevant devices, or given specific paths or mount points to show only those. Output can be sorted by keys such as size, usage, type or filesystem, and columns can be chosen with an output option. Devices can be grouped into tables (local, network, fuse, special, loops, binds) and filtered by table, filesystem type or mount point, including wildcards. It can also switch to inode information, color-code availability and usage using configurable thresholds, and emit JSON.
use_cases: check free disk space on a Linux server
see which mount points are almost full
compare disk usage across local and network filesystems
export disk usage as JSON for scripts
inspect inode usage instead of block usage
view disk space on macOS or Windows terminals
how_to_run: git clone https://github.com/muesli/duf && cd duf && go build (from source, requires Go 1.23+)
stack: Go (1.23 or higher to build from source)
notable: Groups devices into tables such as local, network, fuse, special, loops and binds
Adjusts colors to the terminal theme, with a light theme option
Configurable red/green/yellow thresholds for available space and usage
Wide packaging support across Linux distributions, BSDs, macOS, Windows and Termux
caveats: On oh-my-zsh, an existing 'duf' alias must be removed with unalias before use
Building from source requires Go 1.23 or higher
